correction.text: the whole of Laos from the proclamation of the Lao People's Democratic Republic on 2 December 1975; the 1976 shape unchanged, with the years extended back to 1975

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Communist Laos row begins in 1976 but the infobox gives 'Communist state established: 2 December 1975', the date on which the king abdicated. Only the years change.

229,246 km2 for 1976-2023 against the infobox's 236,800 km2 (no year given): ratio 0.97. The page describes no border change after 1975 and the shape is the same outline in 2024. The gazetteer finds 35 cells (8,852 km2) of modern Laos outside the shape and 35 cells of the shape outside modern Laos (in Thailand and Vietnam), a snapping difference along the Mekong and the watershed frontiers that the page cannot settle ('The Mekong River forms a part of the western boundary with Thailand'; Thai-Lao demarcation was only 96% complete in 2022 per the border-war page).
The same 229,246 km2 outline for the final year; nothing on the page changes it.

region.text: Ban Romklao, 'a dispute over the map made by French surveyors in 1907': Chat Trakan District, Phitsanulok Province, Thailand, against Botene District, Sainyabuli (Xaignabouri) Province, Laos. The page gives no coordinates; the zone is the Phitsanulok-Laos frontier cells of the gazetteer, widened to the Lao side, the researcher's reading

ledger.note: December 1987: Thailand and Laos fight over Ban Romklao. 'In December 1987, however, Thai armed forces occupied the disputed village of Ban Romklao, raising the Thai flag over it'; on 15 December Thai F-5 aircraft bombed Lao positions. Vietnam joined Laos's side on 19 February 1988.

wars.outcome: Infobox 'Thai victory', with 'Return to status quo ante bellum' after the cease-fire of 19 February 1988; the page does not say who ultimately held Ban Romklao.
wars.note: 15 December 1987 to 19 February 1988 (infobox). Lao deaths 195, Thai 150-200 (the page). The Thai-Lao Joint Boundary Commission was established in 1996 'to clarify the 1,810-kilometre boundary', and 'as of 2022, 96% of the land border' had been demarcated.

certainty.note: The frontiers follow the French-era survey lines and the Mekong, and the Thai-Lao boundary has been demarcated since the Joint Boundary Commission of 1996 (96% in 2022). The exception is the Ban Romklao area in Chat Trakan and Botene, disputed over the 1907 French map until the cease-fire of 1988 and after.

notes: The Cliopatria shape (1976 and 2024) is one outline and the state's only border event on the pages is the 1987-88 Ban Romklao war, which returned to the status quo; the new 1975 keyframe extends the shape back to the proclamation on 2 December 1975 (the Kingdom of Laos dossier ends the same month). The shape and modern Laos differ by 35 cells each way (see the keyframe). Page budget (1-2) was spent on the Laos and Thai-Laotian Border War articles. The Laos page gives no dates for the treaty of friendship and cooperation with Vietnam ('a treaty signed in 1977') or for the Vietnamese troops ('In 1979, there were 50,000 PAVN troops stationed in Laos'), and Laos was a Vietnamese client in these years: the vassal_start/vassal_end pair belongs in the socialist-republic-of-vietnam dossier with this state as counterpart, with a page that dates it. The Hmong insurgency ('The conflict between Hmong rebels and Laos continued in certain areas') has no years on the page and is not an event. The Pathet Lao as a rebel state (the kingdom-of-laos dossier names it a successor and contests with it) needs its own dossier from the additions batch. The 1987 zone is a reading: the page names districts and provinces but no coordinates. Wikidata Q819 is Laos as a whole; no other Cliopatria row shares it. The 'united-states-of-america' neighbour listed in the seed for 1976-2005 is Cliopatria's United States row 1967-2005, whose shape contains 551 cells of southern Vietnam (see the republic-of-vietnam notes), not a border with Laos (the intersection with the Laos shape is empty); it is ignored.
